main.result_summary: I consolidated week 1999-W49 (messages m00002–m00009) in one commit, `9257899`. Lint and the sleep audit were both green before I committed. I didn't push, because the run instructions said the runner pushes after its own checks. The 5 new topics are naphtha cap pricing for the Maharashtra deal (`work/naphtha-caps-maharashtra.md`), Robert Lee's visit on 1999-12-29 at 9:00 (`work/visitors.md`), the EPRM Monte Carlo speaker request, where the owner recommended Stinson Gibner (`industry/eprm-risk-courses.md`), and the research group's move to the 19th floor with office numbers and the rankings Greg approved (`organization/research-group.md`); there are also new entity files for Stinson Gibner and Shirley Crenshaw. Every fact links back to its message. I updated all four indexes, the people index and `state.md`. I added one approval question to `questions.md`: whether Pinnamaneni Krishnarao (who signs "Krishna") is the same person as "Krishna Krishnarao" on the office list; I didn't merge them. `dataset/drops/sleep-002.tsv` is empty, because every message with notes is cited and m00006 and m00009 had no notes. Both inbox logs are now in `memory/archive/inbox/`. The audit first went red because I had added a close-out note to the 1999-12-12 log, and an archived log can't be changed. I removed the note, which nothing required since there were no sleep tasks or overdue questions, and the audit then passed. No file was near its size limit, so the compression quota didn't apply. The one open-ended line (vega VaR) is still valid. Lint still warns that `MEMORY.md` and `AGENTS.md` are over their target size; that existed before this run. The runner's untracked `dataset/runs/sleep-002.transcript.jsonl` is not in the commit.
